Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a Hydrogen-Deuterium Exchange Mass Spectrometry (HDX-MS) study. While HDX-MS involves isotopic labeling (D2O), it is used for structural dynamics rather than traditional quantitative proteomics labeling strategies like TMT or SILAC. The peptide identification was performed using DDA on non-deuterated controls.

scope: To purify SHIP1 proteins, insect cell pellets were thawed in room temperature water and resuspended in buffer containing 30 mM Tris (pH 8.0), 10 mM imidazole, 5% glycerol, 400 mM NaCl, 1 mM PMSF, 2 mM beta-mercaptoethanol (BME), 1 Sigma protease inhibitor tablet per 100 ml of buffer, and 100 μg/ml DNase.
High-speed supernatant (HSS) was pooled and batch bound to 5 to 10 ml of nickel (Ni)–nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA) agarose resin (Qiagen, catalog no.: 30230) at 4 °C for 2 h, stirring in a beaker.
The resin bound to his6-mNG-mSHIP1(ΔCTD) constructs was transferred to a gravity flow column and washed with at least 100 ml of additional wash buffer.
The protein was then eluted with buffer containing 20 mM Tris (pH 8.0), 300 mM imidazole, 400 mM NaCl, 5% glycerol, and 2 mM BME.
HDX reactions comparing mNG-SHIP1(ΔCTD) ± 40 μM pY peptide were carried out in a 10 μl reaction volume containing 15 pmol (1.5 μM) of mNG-SHIP1(ΔCTD).
peptide identification was carried out by using a false discovery–based approach using a database of purified proteins and known contaminants.
